previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history including sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic small bowel obstructions, and line-associated DVTs presented with acute epigastric pain, nausea, and inability to pass stool or flatus, consistent with a partial bowel obstruction. Abdominal imaging showed air-fluid levels without a transition point, suggesting ileus. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, NG tube decompression, IV fluids, and electrolyte repletion. Her symptoms improved by hospital day 2 with return of bowel function, allowing NG tube removal and advancement to a regular diet. Due to difficult IV access, a PICC line was placed, which led to transient right arm neuropathic pain managed with a lidocaine patch and increased gabapentin. She remained stable, ambulatory, and pain-controlled, and was discharged home with follow-up plans. No signs of recurrent obstruction or complications were noted at discharge.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ lady who was admitted to the general 
surgery service at the ___ for 
management of recurrent small bowel obstruction. After her 
transfer from the outside hospital and arrival to the surgical 
service, she was started on IVF, given bowel rest, IV pain 
medication and the NGT placed at the OSH was left in place for 
gastric decompression. 

For the first week of her stay, the patient showed no return of 
bowel function and continued to have high bilious NGT output. 
Her prior TPN was continued to bolster her nutritional status.  
After extensive discussions among our team, we determined that 
given her CT findings and substantial history of abdominal 
surgeries, surgical intervention would not be in her best 
interest. Starting the following week, she demonstrated mild 
return of bowel function and was passing very small amounts of 
flatus in the continued presence of high volume bilious NGT 
output. This was promoted by two doses of methylnaltrexone 
though she did not symptomatically feel better in terms of pain; 
the medication was therefore not continued. A GI consult was 
obtained and recommended a small bowel follow-through which 
demonstrated slow passage of contrast through the upper to mid 
jejunum but eventual contrast passage without transition point. 
Based upon these findings and her lack of clinical improvement, 
the GI service performed a push enteroscopy which demonstrated 
dilated jejunum with some sharp angulations but no narrowed 
areas amenable to dilations; thus, no further intervention was 
performed. The ___ team was consulted and placed a Gtube the 
following day to facilitate decompression at home. She will be 
sent home with daily TPN cycled; labs will be checked weekly by 
___. The TPN volume was increased during her stay to maximize 
her hydration. She was additionally started on free water 
flushes per her Gtube to further maintain adequate hydration, 
which were titrated to 150cc q8 hours and well tolerated. She 
was allowed sips of any clear liquids ___ cups every 8 hours), 
which she tolerated well and can continue at home while 
monitoring her abdominal distension. 

From a neurological perspective, the patient developed new 
word-finding difficulties and subjective right-sided weakness on 
HD13. She underwent a non-contrast CT head which was negative 
for acute process. Her labwork was unrevealing. Given her 
history of prior stroke, she was seen by the neurology service; 
they recommended EEG which showed diffuse left-sided swelling, 
potentially attributable to prior stroke, but no seizure 
activity. They also recommended a CTA head/neck; she required 
placement of a midline by ___ to faciliate the contrast for the 
CTA head/neck that was removed prior to discharge. CTA head/neck 
showed chronic prior stroke but no new findings and normal 
carotid/vertebral vasculature. Her weakness resolved over time 
but she continued to have persistent though improved 
word-finding difficulties. Neurology recommended no intervention 
and outpatient follow-up with her neurologist. 

Her xarelto (for lower extremity DVT) was initially held during 
her stay due to the need for potential intervention but she was 
restarted on therapeutic lovenox once further intervention was 
deemed unlikely. She will continue therapeutic lovenox at home 
due to concern that she may not fully absorb the enteral 
eliquis. She will continue lovenox to complete the 6-month 
course as previously prescribed by her primary doctor.  

In terms of her pain control, she was initially treated with 
intermittent IV dilauadid. A chronic pain service consult was 
obtained prior to discharge to optimize her home regimen given 
her complicated history refractory to multiple modalities. She 
was trialed on PR dilaudid with good relief and weaned off IV 
dilaudid. She will continue on dilaudid suppositories at home as 
needed and follow up with a chronic pain specialist for renewal. 


She has planned follow up with a GI surgeon in ___, where 
she is planning to move with her husband. The GI surgeon will 
coordinate her home TPN there as well as help her find a primary 
care physician, ___, and neurologist.

___ gastrostomy catheter was advanced over the wire into position. The
catheter was secured by forming the retaining loop in the stomach after
confirming the position of the catheter with a contrast injection. The
catheter was then flushed, capped and secured to the skin with 0-silk sutures.
Sterile dressings were applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
complications.

PROCEDURE:

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right
brachial vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a
micropuncture set. Permanent ultrasound images were obtained before and after

in the subclavian vein under fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter
was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest. The peel-away sheath
and guidewire were then removed. The catheter was secured to the skin,
flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

subclavian vein.
